Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(M_n=\max A_n\).

First, taking \(i=j\) gives

\[
|A_i|=|A_i\cap A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i,
\]

so \(M_n\ge n\) for every \(n\).

For any \(1\le a<b\),

\[
|A_a\cup A_b|=a+b-\gcd(a,b).
\]

Since \(\max(A_a\cup A_b)=\max(M_a,M_b)\), we have

\[
\max(M_a,M_b)\ge a+b-\gcd(a,b).
\]

Also \(\min(M_a,M_b)\ge a\). Hence

\[
M_a+M_b\ge a+b-\gcd(a,b)+a.
\]

The positive divisors of \(250\) are

\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250.
\]

Applying the inequality to the pairs \((2,5)\), \((10,25)\), \((50,125)\), and using \(M_1\ge1\), \(M_{250}\ge250\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d
&=M_1+(M_2+M_5)+(M_{10}+M_{25})+(M_{50}+M_{125})+M_{250}\\
&\ge 1+(2+5-1+2)+(10+25-5+10)+(50+125-25+50)+250\\
&=1+8+40+200+250\\
&=499.
\end{aligned}
\]

So the desired sum is at least \(499\).

It remains to show this is attainable. Let \(\varphi\) be Euler’s totient function. For each positive integer \(m\), choose \(\varphi(m)\) distinct positive integers, and for \(m\mid 250\) choose them as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
m & \text{assigned integers} \\
\hline
1 & \{1\}\\
2 & \{2\}\\
5 & \{3,4,5,6\}\\
10 & \{7,8,9,10\}\\
25 & \{11,\dots,30\}\\
50 & \{31,\dots,50\}\\
125 & \{51,\dots,150\}\\
250 & \{151,\dots,250\}
\end{array}
\]

For \(m\nmid 250\), assign the required \(\varphi(m)\) unused integers greater than \(250\).

Define

\[
A_n=\bigcup_{m\mid n} B_m,
\]

where \(B_m\) is the set of assigned integers for \(m\). Then

\[
|A_n|=\sum_{m\mid n}\varphi(m)=n.
\]

Also,

\[
A_i\cap A_j=\bigcup_{m\mid i,\ m\mid j}B_m=\bigcup_{m\mid \gcd(i,j)}B_m=A_{\gcd(i,j)},
\]

so

\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\gcd(i,j).
\]

Thus this is a valid sequence. For divisors \(d\mid 250\), the maximum values are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d & 1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\
\hline
\max A_d & 1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]

and their sum is

\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
